topic: Semantic Kernel Agent RCE Vulnerabilities Guide 2026

cves.title: Semantic Kernel Python SDK InMemoryVectorStore RCE
cves.description: Remote code execution via unsafe eval() in InMemoryVectorStore filter. AI model-controlled input interpolated into Python lambda string and passed to eval(). AST blocklist bypassed via class hierarchy traversal (BuiltinImporter → load_module → os.system).
cves.attack_vector: Prompt injection → search plugin → crafted filter parameter → eval() sink → RCE
cves.fix: AST node-type allowlist, function call allowlist, dangerous attributes blocklist, name node restriction. Upgrade to >=1.39.4.

cves.title: Semantic Kernel .NET SDK SessionsPythonPlugin Arbitrary File Write
cves.description: DownloadFileAsync accidentally marked with [KernelFunction] attribute, exposing it as an AI-callable tool. No path validation on localFilePath parameter allowed writing files to arbitrary host locations (e.g., Windows Startup folder).
cves.attack_vector: Prompt injection → agent calls DownloadFileAsync → file written to host Startup folder → RCE on next sign-in
cves.fix: Removed [KernelFunction] attribute, added path validation via ValidateLocalPathForDownload(). Upgrade to >=1.71.0.

key_insights: Prompt injection escalates from content risk to host compromise when agents are wired to tools
AI models are not security boundaries — every tool parameter the model can influence is attacker-controlled input
Python eval() with blocklist security is inherently fragile in dynamic languages like Python
Function exposure via attributes (e.g., [KernelFunction]) creates unintentional attack surface
Both CVEs affect Semantic Kernel, one of the most widely-used agent frameworks with 27K+ GitHub stars
mitigation_recommendations: Upgrade Python SDK to >=1.39.4 and .NET SDK to >=1.71.0
Treat all AI-influenced parameters as untrusted input
Monitor agent host processes for suspicious child processes (cmd.exe, powershell, etc.)
Use Microsoft Defender advanced hunting queries for post-exploitation detection
Apply Function Invocation Filters for path validation on file operations

angle_for_blog: This is a defining moment for AI agent security. Unlike traditional web vulnerabilities, these CVEs show that prompt injection is no longer a content-quality issue — it's a code execution primitive. The guide should position Semantic Kernel as the case study for why every agent framework needs input sanitization at the tool boundary, not just the model layer. Focus on: (1) technical breakdown of how eval() bypass works, (2) the .NET sandbox escape chain, (3) actionable mitigation checklist, and (4) broader industry implications for LangChain, CrewAI, and other frameworks.
